note: Milestone 70, 70T: which browser specs reach the app only through window.GuardianForms.testing (or the real UI), checked by tests/unit/ms70-70T-guard.spec.js, and what converting them found. A write moved from a raw patch to setField() or the real UI may make a test fail that passed before: that is a finding about today's test, recorded here with its resolution, never suppressed (decision D9).

exempt.why: Drives a Guardian Forms build from before Milestone 70, which has no GuardianForms namespace, through that build's own window globals: the mixed-version characterization runs such a build beside this tree on purpose. Used by tests/e2e/mixed-version.characterization.spec.ts alone; removed once production runs a post-70 build.

findings.what: Seven 'the sidebar mark turned green' checks were toHaveClass(/complete/), which also matches the class 'incomplete' -- they could not fail, so a page that never turned green passed.
findings.resolution: Anchored to /\bcomplete\b/ on the branch and on master (the defect predates Milestone 70). If a mark does not really turn green, the corrected check now says so.

findings.what: After answering the depository question the test forced the sidebar to redraw (updateNavDots()) before checking the mark -- a render the app must do on its own when a filer answers (D9).
findings.resolution: The forced redraw is gone; the mark is checked exactly as a filer would see it after the click.

findings.what: Three tests proved deleted window.* bridges stay deleted by naming them in the page (typeof window.addGuardian and kin) -- a browser spec naming app globals, which the 70T guard forbids even to prove them absent.
findings.resolution: The pins moved to tests/unit/removed-window-bridges.spec.js, read from the source by the window-bridge audit (window.X =, legacy top-level functions, Object.defineProperty); seen failing for a re-added function, a re-added defineProperty and a renamed kept bridge. Recorded in the assertion-count drop log.

findings.what: Every test called case-resolver.js's pure functions through their window bridges, and several depend on object identity (resolveCase() returning the very Case createCase() made), which copies from GuardianForms.testing cannot show.
findings.resolution: Moved to tests/unit/case-resolver.spec.js by direct import: same five tests, same 18 expects; seen failing with the caseId branch disabled.

findings.what: The two caption checks called legacy-app.js's circuitCourtCaption(), which nothing in the app calls -- the caption a filer receives, the court PDF's, went unchecked for a blank county. The carry-over checks called carryOverFields() on an Annual-to-Annual pairing the Add Filing dialog does not offer.
findings.resolution: Captions are read from the generated Annual PDF; carry-over goes through the real dialog (Annual to Plan Annual). circuitCourtCaption() now has no consumer at all: its disposition becomes delete-as-dead, for 70B.

findings.what: The 'a blank UCN is never reported as missing' check ran whichever validator happened to be loaded first (validateGuardian || validateAnnual || ...), not necessarily the open filing type's -- for some types it could have checked the wrong form.
findings.resolution: It runs the open filing's own validator (validate.open()).

findings.what: The stale-delegate probes replaced an app function with a counter (openFloridaCourtPortal, showPickPartyModal) and asserted zero -- a probe never shown to reach a live delegate.
findings.resolution: Each watches what the handler does (a window opening; the Link to Shared Record dialog) and adds a control: with the feature mounted, the same probe does trigger it.

findings.what: The tests normalized hand-built data by calling normalizeWardData() themselves, so they proved the function, not that stored older data is normalized when a filer opens it.
findings.resolution: The older shape is stored on the filing, which is closed and opened again (activateWard() -> setD() runs the normalizer); the empty sentinel is checked after leaving for the dashboard.

findings.what: Its old side runs a pre-Milestone-70 build, which has no GuardianForms; a mechanical conversion drove both builds through the adapter, which the old one cannot answer.
findings.resolution: Each tab is driven through its own build: this tree through GuardianForms.testing (support/app-driver.ts), the old one through its own globals in support/pre-70-build.ts -- the one file exempt from the guard, with its reason and its single permitted importer checked.

findings.what: The adapter exposed commitCoverCounty() as a shared-record command, although the reviewed design classes it real-UI: a spec could give the ward Party a county no filer's click produced.
findings.resolution: Removed; setup that needs the ward Party's county chooses it through the real Cover combobox (target.ts chooseCoverCounty()).

findings.what: The recorded design still carried the rules from before two 70T schema corrections, and its spec compared only names, so the drift went unnoticed.
findings.resolution: Regenerated; tests/unit/ms70-testing-adapter-design.spec.js now requires the recorded design to equal what the rules produce (seen failing against the stale file).

findings.what: Each read `caseFile.wards` as a bare name inside page.evaluate() -- window.caseFile, reached without writing `window` -- and the first 70T guard saw only window member access, so two of them were already counted as converted.
findings.resolution: Read through GuardianForms.testing.snapshot(). The inventory now reports free identifiers that name anything src/ can put on window, and the guard fails on them (seen failing on exactly these files).

findings.what: The mechanical converter turned Object.assign(window.D.x, row) into Object.assign(GuardianForms.testing.field('x'), row): a write into a copy that changes nothing. In the remuneration spec the 'a complete row satisfies Part VII' setup had silently done nothing since its conversion.
findings.resolution: Both now patch the filing (setup, D9). The inventory reports any write into a value GuardianForms.testing returned -- direct, Object.assign, mutator or delete, through a `t` alias or not -- and the guard fails on it (seen failing with the remuneration write restored).

findings.what: The converter replaced live objects with copies throughout (resolveParty(id) === party, caseFile.wards.push(...)), so its identity checks compared copies and its setup wrote into them.
findings.resolution: Rebuilt from the committed version: the 26 pure-logic tests run on the modules in tests/unit/party-resolver.spec.js (same bodies, 165 expects; seen failing with the merge tombstone ignored); the three .sav round trips stay in the browser, with the carry-over through the real Add Filing dialog.

findings.what: Two tests used schedule keys no page renders ('annualSchA', 'guardianSchA1'): they proved a supporting-documents slot no filer ever sees.
findings.resolution: They use Schedule A's real sections ('schA' on /scha, 'a1' on /a1) and read what the Supporting Documents section shows after each period change.

findings.what: The Rename Ward dialog was tested by calling showRenameWardModal(); no button has opened it since the Milestone 36 dashboard consolidation (e5fb9cf). The no-active-filing state was staged by setting three globals by hand.
findings.resolution: The rename steps are dropped and the dialog, showRenameWardModal() and the dead shell/dashboard 'rename-ward' cases are handed to 70B as delete-as-dead. The state is reached by closing the filing; deletes go through the dashboard's Delete buttons.

findings.what: The 'Open Data File' test called triggerImportZip(), which no button has called since Milestone 41B consolidated save and backup to two buttons (4cd5723); the sidebar button runs triggerOpenBackupSav().
findings.resolution: The test clicks the real Open Backup button; triggerImportZip() is handed to 70B as delete-as-dead. saveBlobAs()'s AbortError contract moved to tests/unit/case-file.spec.js.

findings.what: The Slice 19E drift guard assigned its sentinel filing to window.D with no filing open -- a state the app never reaches -- and its architecture half read window.calcTotalsAnnual.
findings.resolution: The sentinel becomes a real Annual filing, closed and reopened so the load path prepares it; balance comes from status.annualReconcile(). The one-calculator claim is checked on the module graph in tests/unit/annual-accounting-totals.spec.js (seen failing both ways).

findings.what: Jump targets were proved by calling focusFieldByPath(); the Initial Plan attorney predicate by calling it through window; the conversion attestation reset by calling the four mappers on hand-built destinations (its 'addresses still migrate' was collected but never asserted); Part XI normalization by calling normalizeWardData() on bare objects.
findings.resolution: A jump link is dispatched through the app's own delegate; the predicate has tests/unit/attorney-block.spec.js; the real conversions run (Convert Filing) and the recipient is asserted to migrate; the older shapes are stored and the filing reopened.

findings.what: Behavior was reached by calling app functions or instrumenting live objects: a setter on the live filing to order save-before-download, stubbed showPickPartyModal(), showWardLockedModal()/showAddWardModal()/showConvertWardModal() called directly, saveBackupNow()/saveBlobAs()/finishSingleWardExport() called directly.
findings.resolution: Each goes through what a filer does or sees: the filing's state at the moment the download starts; the Link to Shared Record dialog opening (with a control); a real Web Lock held on the filing; the dashboard's New Filing, Convert, Backup and the sidebar's Save Backup buttons.

findings.what: 'Unknown fragment names are rejected without a request' called window.loadFragment() in the page.
findings.resolution: Checked on src/fragment-loader.js directly in tests/unit/fragment-loader.spec.js, every request recorded, with a control that the allowlisted fragment is fetched (seen failing with the allowlist removed).

findings.what: Its conversion (batch 2) wrote the long guardian addresses through a loop variable into a snapshot copy and then only saved: the setup changed nothing, so four tests had no addresses to measure. The guard could not see it -- the write went through `g`, not the copy's own name. Found by 70T's gate run.
findings.resolution: The copy is written back (replaceFiling). The inventory now follows a copy held in a variable through what is derived from it (members, for-of items, array-callback parameters, `||` fallbacks) and reports a write unless the copy is handed on; a test that writes a copy on purpose marks the declaring line `copy-write: deliberate` (tests/e2e/testing-adapter.spec.ts). Seen failing on this exact defect restored.

findings.what: Rendering the Supporting Documents section runs the app's PDF check on each stored file; the seeded file records had no content, so the app rightly marked one 'not a readable PDF'. The old test never rendered, so its seed never had to be realistic. Found by 70T's gate run.
findings.resolution: Two real PDFs (6 and 7 pages, built with pdf-lib) are uploaded through the section's own file control, and the page counts the app reads are asserted.

findings.what: The new positive control for the stale-delegate probe clicked the Link to Shared Record dialog's Cancel while the supporting-documentation prompt (Milestone 57C-R) -- raised by the loop's Schedule B-2 rows -- sat on top of it. Found by 70T's gate run.
findings.resolution: The control dismisses that prompt first (dismissScheduleDocPrompt(), a no-op when none is showing).
